title: CRLR/100/2018 of Manish Rawat Vs State Of Uttarakhand AND ANOTHER

paras.text:
CRLR No. 100 of 2018
Hon'ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.
Mr. Niranjan Bhatt, Advocate for the revisionist.
Mr. P.S. Bohra, AGA for the State.
Mr. Anil Dabral, Advocate for the private
respondent.
This revision emanates from an order dated
07.03.2018, as passed by the learned Family Court,
Kotdwar, District Pauri Garhwal, wherein the
application filed by the respondent-wife i.e. paper No.
11(kha), invoking the provisions contained under sub
Section (2) of Section 125 Cr.PC for consideration of
the grant of interim maintenance has been disposed of
by the learned Family Court, determining the
maintenance payable by the revisionist-husband to the
tune of Rs. 1100/- to the respondent-wife and Rs.
5,000/- to the son i.e. total sum of Rs. 6100/- per
month has been made payable by the revisionist to
respondent.
When the revision itself was entertained and
notice was issued to the respondent, the coordinate
Bench of this Court, on 17.04.2018, by way of an
interim arrangement had admitted the revision subject
to the condition that the revisionist remits the amount
of Rs. 5,000/- per month to the respondent-wife.
Since then, the said interim order is operating
and the learned counsel for the revisionist contends
that he is paying the amount as rendered by the
coordinate Bench of this Court on 17.04.2018, but this
fact is disputed by the learned counsel for the
respondent-wife that the amount of maintenance as
determined by the learned Family Court, has not been
remitted by the revisionist and as such no interference
is required to be made by this Court while exercising
its writ jurisdiction.
In case respondent No. 2 has any grievance with
regards to non compliance of the order of maintenance
as modified by the interim order dated 17.04.2018 by
the coordinate Bench of this Court, the recourse
available to the respondent-wife would be by invoking

the appropriate provisions contained under sub Section
(3) of Section 125 Cr.PC because present revision
preferred by the revisionist-husband, no such direction
could be issued for recovering the so-called balance
amount, which the respondent-wife contends that she
was liable to receive could be issued.
In such an eventuality, and even considering the
aspects that this revision is arising out of an
interlocutory order and further there operates an
interim order dated 17.04.2018, keeping this revision
pending would entail unnecessarily hardship to the
litigation on the parties to the present criminal
revision. Hence, while disposing of this criminal
revision, learned Family Court is requested to decide
the application under Section 125 Cr.PC, itself on its
own merits. It is left open to the respondent-wife to
file an appropriate application for claiming any
remittance of the amount which otherwise she was
entitled to receive in pursuance to the impugned order
of maintenance.
Furthermore, this revision stands disposed of
with request to the learned Family Court to decide the
main application under Section 125 Cr.PC on its own
merits within a period of three months from the date of
production of certified copy of this order and for a
period of three months, the interim arrangement as
determined by the coordinate Bench of this Court
dated 17.04.2018 would be continued to operate till the
application under Section 125 Cr.PC itself is decided,
within the aforesaid period.
